text:
maria: Anyone hitting huge auth refresh storms on API 23 emulator? My sample-auth app spun up dozens of refresh calls and the emulator network saturated.

sam: Which refresh path are you on? OkHttp Authenticator or Interceptor-based refresh?

maria: Interceptor-based. We detect 401, call refresh, then replay. But on slow emulator the interceptor seems to re-enter and spawn concurrent refreshes. Logs show repeating requests tagged as (retry).

gloria: That sounds like the re-entrancy + coroutine interplay we saw before. OkHttp Call objects can be reused and multiple threads may get into the Interceptor while a single refresh is still in-flight.

maria: Example logs:
```
I/OkHttp: --> GET /v1/generate
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized (2ms)
I/OkHttp: --> GET /v1/generate (retry)
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized (1ms)
I/OkHttp: --> GET /v1/generate (retry)
```
No WWW-Authenticate header from our backend, so OkHttp "Authenticator" path wouldn't be invoked.

sam: Right — Authenticator relies on server challenge headers (WWW-Authenticate). For bearer flows where the backend omits the header, Authenticator won't help. Interceptor is correct but you must guard refreshes.

gloria: Our recommended pattern in the SDK docs: single refresh lock + tag retried requests to prevent loops. Use a coroutine Mutex and avoid blocking the main thread. Also make refresh have a short timeout so the lock isn't held for long on flaky TLS.

maria: I tried synchronized + blocking and it caused ANRs on emulator. Any minimal coroutine-friendly snippet we can ship?

sam: here's a compact Kotlin pattern we used (bridging coroutines inside Interceptor with runBlocking):
```kotlin
private val refreshMutex = Mutex()
intercept(chain) { // pseudocode
  val req = chain.request()
  val resp = chain.proceed(req)
  if (resp.code == 401 && req.header("X-Authed-Retry") == null) {
    runBlocking {
      if (!refreshMutex.isLocked) {
        refreshMutex.withLock { authService.refreshSync() }
      }
    }
    val newReq = req.newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${tokenStore.token}")
      .header("X-Authed-Retry", "1")
      .build()
    return chain.proceed(newReq)
  }
  return resp
}
```
Escape hatch: the `X-Authed-Retry` header prevents the interceptor from retrying repeatedly.

gloria: A few related gotchas we should document in quickstart: 1) don't rely on OkHttp Authenticator unless backend sends challenge headers, 2) `retryOnConnectionFailure(true)` can mask TLS flakiness and cause duplicate refresh attempts, 3) on older Android (<API 24) TLS handshakes may be flaky on emulators — suggest ProviderInstaller/Conscrypt or test on GMS images.

maria: Also seeing TLS handshake timeouts during refresh on API 23. Those timeouts block the mutex and cause bursts when they finally fail. Would tuning timeouts per-call help?

sam: Yes. Configure a shorter callTimeout/readTimeout for the refresh client so it fails fast and frees the mutex. Example: build a small OkHttpClient just for token refresh with callTimeout=5s.

gloria: Another practical addition: emit a telemetry count when > 3 concurrent refresh attempts are observed. That helps detect if people hit this in the wild. We'll gate it behind a feature flag.

devex-bot: Note: sample-auth PR 542 created (GuardedAuthInterceptor + tests) | CI artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/542

maria: I'll open a tiny PR to sdk-android adding GuardedAuthInterceptor, a sample change, an emulator connectedAndroidTest for API 23, and a short README note about TLS providers. Draft at https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-android/pull/542

sam: Please include a unit test that simulates 10 concurrent 401 responses and asserts only a single call to the auth server. That caught a race in an earlier variant.

gloria: Also add an integration suggestion: if you must use Authenticator, ensure your backend emits a proper WWW-Authenticate header and be aware of platform differences. Prefer interceptor-pattern for most bearer flows.

maria: Will add a lightweight metric (concurrent_refresh_attempts) and a short recipe in quickstart. Plan to ship as a patch release.

sam: SGTM. I can help with the CI emulator image so flakes are reproducible. :thumbsup: 

maria: Thanks all — I'll run connectedAndroidTest on a clean API 23 image and update the PR with results. Reminder from bot: `./gradlew :samples:sample-auth:connectedAndroidTest` before merging.
